items.name: Watchdog checkpoint coalescing
items.contract: Pure helper internal/builderloop/watchdog_coalesce.go exposes type Decision string with constants DecisionFirst="first", DecisionAmend="amend", DecisionNoop="noop"; type CheckpointState struct{LastCheckpointAt time.Time; LastSubject string; WindowID string}; type CoalesceConfig struct{WindowSeconds int; Dirty bool; NextWindowID func() string} and one function DecideCheckpoint(now time.Time, st CheckpointState, cfg CoalesceConfig) (Decision, CheckpointState). Window math: windowSeconds <= 0 falls back to 600. Algorithm: when cfg.Dirty is false, return DecisionNoop and the input state unchanged. When cfg.Dirty is true and (st.WindowID == "" OR now.Sub(st.LastCheckpointAt) >= window), return DecisionFirst with state {LastCheckpointAt: now, LastSubject: st.LastSubject (caller fills), WindowID: cfg.NextWindowID()}. Otherwise (cfg.Dirty and inside the window) return DecisionAmend with state {LastCheckpointAt: now, LastSubject: st.LastSubject, WindowID: st.WindowID} (preserve the existing WindowID). No git invocation, no shell-script change, no live filesystem mutation in this slice; cfg.NextWindowID is the only source of new IDs and is supplied by the caller (typically a small monotonic counter or a uuid stub in tests).
items.degraded_mode: Watchdog status reports checkpoint_coalesce_active, checkpoint_coalesce_window_seconds, and the existing dirty-worktree checkpoint commit ID instead of emitting a fresh commit on every tick.
ready_when: Watchdog dirty-worktree checkpointing is in place (commit ff96a5d94) and emits a record_run_health event we can key off of.
Tests can use a fake clock and an in-memory git repo or a synthetic commit-recorder seam — no live system clock or systemd is required.
not_ready_when: The slice changes the watchdog stall threshold, the dead-process detection, or the planner cadence.
The slice silently drops the dirty-worktree checkpoint when a stall is real — the first tick of every distinct stall window must still produce a single observable checkpoint.
acceptance: TestDecideCheckpoint_FirstTickInFreshWindowReturnsFirst: empty state, cfg.Dirty=true, NextWindowID=()=>"w-1" returns (DecisionFirst, {LastCheckpointAt: now, WindowID: "w-1"}).

TestDecideCheckpoint_LaterTickInsideWindowReturnsAmend: prior state {LastCheckpointAt: now-30s, WindowID: "w-1"}, cfg.Dirty=true, windowSeconds=600 returns (DecisionAmend, {LastCheckpointAt: now, WindowID: "w-1"}); NextWindowID is NOT called.

TestDecideCheckpoint_LaterTickPastWindowReturnsFirst: prior state {LastCheckpointAt: now-601s, WindowID: "w-1"}, cfg.Dirty=true, windowSeconds=600, NextWindowID=()=>"w-2" returns (DecisionFirst, {LastCheckpointAt: now, WindowID: "w-2"}).
TestDecideCheckpoint_NoopWhenNotDirty: any prior state, cfg.Dirty=false returns (DecisionNoop, prior state unchanged); NextWindowID is NOT called.
TestDecideCheckpoint_DefaultWindowWhenZeroOrNegative: cfg.WindowSeconds=0 and cfg.WindowSeconds=-5 both behave like windowSeconds=600.
Helper is a pure function with no time.Now, no git invocation, no os.* calls — caller passes both the clock (now) and the dirty flag (cfg.Dirty) and the WindowID generator (cfg.NextWindowID).
items.note: Complete: TDD landed the pure DecideCheckpoint helper and fake-clock fixtures for first checkpoint, in-window amend, post-window rotation, no-dirty noop, and the 600-second fallback for zero/negative window sizes. Pure-Go decider only — shell-script wiring at scripts/orchestrator/watchdog.sh is OUT of scope and will be a separate row that imports DecideCheckpoint via a small stub binary.
done_signal: internal/builderloop/watchdog_coalesce_test.go fixtures prove first/amend/first-after-rotation/noop decisions across a fake clock with no live git or systemd.

provenance.note: Reduces the 74-commit/28-min checkpoint storm observed overnight 2026-04-25 → 2026-04-26 to ≤1 commit per stall window.

items.name: Watchdog dead-process vs slow-progress separation
items.contract: TDD packet for a missing pure helper; create exactly two files and do not wire them into the watchdog loop. STEP 1: cd into the repo root and run `ls internal/builderloop/watchdog_state*.go` — both files must be absent before the worker writes them. STEP 2: write internal/builderloop/watchdog_state_test.go in package builderloop with one TestDiagnose function holding a t.Run-driven table. The subtests are named exactly zero_pid_dead, pid_not_live_after_dead_threshold, live_after_slow_threshold, dead_wins_when_both_thresholds_fire, healthy_recent_live, and pid_live_silent_for_a_year_is_slow_not_dead. Use a fixed time anchor `now := time.Date(2026,4,26,18,0,0,0,time.UTC)` and pass deadAfter=120*time.Second, slowAfter=600*time.Second. STEP 3: write internal/builderloop/watchdog_state.go exposing type Verdict string with constants VerdictHealthy="healthy", VerdictSlow="slow", VerdictDead="dead"; type WorkerVitals struct{PID int; LastCommitAt time.Time; PIDIsLive bool}; and func Diagnose(now time.Time, v WorkerVitals, deadAfter, slowAfter time.Duration) Verdict. Verdict precedence (evaluate in this order): if v.PID==0 return VerdictDead; let elapsed := now.Sub(v.LastCommitAt); if !v.PIDIsLive && elapsed>=deadAfter return VerdictDead; if v.PIDIsLive && elapsed>=slowAfter return VerdictSlow; otherwise return VerdictHealthy. STEP 4: the helper uses only caller-injected now and PIDIsLive — no os.FindProcess, signal delivery, time.Now, goroutines, watchdog wiring, config validation, or imports beyond `time`.
items.degraded_mode: Watchdog status reports worker_state ∈ {alive_progressing, alive_silent, dead, unknown} and the threshold each one tripped; record_run_health carries the worker_state and which threshold (dead_after_seconds, silent_after_seconds) fired.

items.name: Builder-loop self-improvement vs user-feature ratio metric
items.contract: TDD packet for a missing pure helper; create exactly two files and do not parse the live ledger. STEP 1: cd into the repo root and run `ls internal/builderloop/ship_ratio*.go` — both files must be absent before the worker writes them. STEP 2: write internal/builderloop/ship_ratio_test.go in package builderloop with two top-level test functions. TestClassifySubphase uses a t.Run-driven table with named subtests bare_1c, path_1c, bare_5o, path_5o, control_plane_prefix, user_feature_4a, user_feature_4h, user_feature_6a, user_feature_7b, blank_input, whitespace_only, and unknown_99x; each asserts ClassifySubphase returns the expected RowKind. TestComputeShipRatio uses a fixed time anchor `now := time.Date(2026,4,26,18,0,0,0,time.UTC)` and a 24h window; subtests inclusive_window_start, future_event_excluded, per_kind_counts, and zero_events_returns_zero_total. STEP 3: write internal/builderloop/ship_ratio.go exposing type RowKind string with constants RowKindSelfImprovement="self_improvement", RowKindUserFeature="user_feature", RowKindUnclassified="unclassified"; type ShippedRowEvent struct{SubphaseID string; ShippedAt time.Time}; type ShipRatio struct{SelfImprovement int; UserFeature int; Unclassified int; Total int}; func ClassifySubphase(subphaseID string) RowKind; and func ComputeShipRatio(events []ShippedRowEvent, window time.Duration, now time.Time) ShipRatio. ClassifySubphase trims spaces, splits on "/" and inspects the second segment if the first is a phase number ("1","4","5","6","7"), and treats bare "1.C", "5.O", and any string with prefix "control-plane/" as RowKindSelfImprovement. "4.A", "4.H", "6.*", "7.*" map to RowKindUserFeature; everything else (including blank input) returns RowKindUnclassified. ComputeShipRatio is a pure aggregator over the provided slice. STEP 4: no file I/O, no ledger parsing, no record_run_health emission, no goroutines, no live clock; imports only `strings` and `time` plus `testing` in the test file.

items.name: Durable worker abort-slot recovery safety net
items.contract: Gormes durable worker execution loop propagates timed-out jobs into handler cancellation and uses a bounded grace timer to free the worker slot with auditable recovery evidence if the handler ignores cancellation
items.degraded_mode: Durable-worker status reports abort_signal_sent, abort_slot_recovered, handler_ignored_abort, or abort_recovery_unavailable instead of leaving capacity wedged.
ready_when: A Gormes durable worker execution loop exists that claims jobs from the SQLite ledger and invokes a handler through context.Context.

The slice changes live delegate_task behavior, cron execution semantics, or builder-loop backend execution.
acceptance: TestDurableWorker_TimeoutPropagatesCancel seeds a claimed job with a short timeout, runs a fake handler that observes ctx.Done, and asserts the ledger records aborted/dead evidence plus abort_signal_sent status.

TestDurableWorker_IgnoredAbortReleasesSlot runs a fake handler that blocks after ctx cancellation; after the injected grace clock fires, worker capacity is released, abort_slot_recovered is recorded once, and the handler cannot later double-complete the job.
TestDurableWorker_ClaimsNextJobAfterRecovery proves a second waiting job can be claimed after recovery from the ignored-abort handler.
Doctor/status fixtures expose handler_ignored_abort and abort_recovery_unavailable without requiring operators to inspect raw ledger rows.
items.note: Complete: TDD landed internal/subagent/durable_worker_abort_test.go over the Go-native DurableWorker.RunOne seam. Timed-out runs now cancel the handler context, record abort_signal_sent audit evidence, terminally cancel the durable job with lock release, and, when a handler ignores cancellation, use an injected bounded grace timer to record handler_ignored_abort plus one-shot abort_slot_recovered evidence before returning capacity. Late handler returns cannot double-complete recovered jobs, a follow-up waiting job can be claimed after recovery, and doctor/status now exposes abort recovery counts including abort_recovery_unavailable.
done_signal: Durable worker fixtures prove timeout cancellation reaches handlers, ignored handlers free capacity through a one-shot grace recovery, the next job can claim, and doctor/status expose abort recovery evidence.

items.name: Gateway persistent goal loop + continuation judge
items.contract: Gormes ports Hermes `/goal` as a session-scoped gateway loop: goals persist in session metadata, support status/pause/resume/clear/done states and a max-turn budget, setting a goal queues the first turn, post-turn evaluation uses a fail-open auxiliary judge, continuation prompts are queued only when the judge says continue, user messages take priority and pause the loop for that turn, and mid-run `/goal` only allows safe inspection/control commands.
items.degraded_mode: Missing session metadata, unavailable auxiliary judge, malformed judge JSON, exhausted budgets, queue failures, or active-turn unsafe goal changes return goal_* evidence and continue safely without wedging the session, losing the user message, or starting an unbounded loop.
ready_when: Gateway-handled slash commands bypass active-session guard is complete, so safe mid-run command routing exists.

Session metadata and active-turn queue tests can run with fake stores, fake auxiliary judge clients, and fake gateway events; no provider, live gateway transport, or Hermes Python runtime is required.
`/goal` is currently recognized but unavailable, so this row can flip the command only after behavior is fixture-locked.
not_ready_when: The slice calls a live auxiliary model in tests, stores goal state globally instead of per session, or runs continuations without a budget.
User-submitted messages are appended behind an automatic goal continuation instead of taking priority.
Setting a new arbitrary goal mid-run bypasses the active-turn guard.
blocked_by: Gateway-handled slash commands bypass active-session guard
acceptance: TestGoalStatePersistsPerSession proves set/status/pause/resume/clear/done state round-trips through session metadata and a second manager sees the active goal.
TestGoalJudgeFailOpen proves empty responses, malformed JSON, missing auxiliary clients, and judge errors return continue evidence rather than skipping or failing the session.
TestGatewayGoalCommandQueuesInitialTurn proves `/goal ship it` stores the goal and enqueues the first submit through the existing session route.

TestGatewayGoalPostTurnContinuationBudget proves done stops, continue queues exactly one bounded continuation prompt, budget exhaustion pauses with evidence, and user messages pause continuation for that turn.
TestGatewayGoalActiveTurnPolicy proves mid-run status/pause/resume/clear are allowed while setting a new goal returns safe busy evidence.

done_signal: Gateway and session fixtures prove `/goal` persists per session, controls active goals, fail-open judges completion, and queues bounded continuations without live providers.

items.name: Azure Foundry probe — path sniffing
items.contract: TDD packet for a missing pure helper; create exactly two files and do not edit the already validated /models probe. First add internal/hermes/azure_foundry_path_sniff_test.go in package hermes with TestClassifyAzurePath table subtests named exact_anthropic, trailing_anthropic, nested_anthropic, mixed_case, bare_host_unknown, openai_path_unknown, substring_false_positives, and empty_and_malformed_unknown. Then add internal/hermes/azure_foundry_path_sniff.go exposing ClassifyAzurePath(rawURL string) AzureTransport that reuses the AzureTransport type/constants from internal/hermes/azure_foundry_models_probe.go. items.name: Ephemeral prefill messages file injection
items.contract: Port Hermes' ephemeral prefill-message behavior into the native Go turn path. Gormes loads a JSON array of message objects from an explicit prefill file setting, resolves relative paths from the Gormes runtime home while preserving Hermes-compatible env/config aliases, validates the payload without logging content, and injects copies of those messages into provider-bound API messages immediately after the effective system prompt and before conversation history/user input. Prefill messages are API-call-time only: they must not be written to session history, channel transcripts, memory/Goncho stores, debug logs, or visible TUI/gateway output.

not_ready_when: The slice persists prefill messages to sessions, memory, transcript history, debug bundles, logs, or channel-visible text.

The slice reads the operator's live home directory in tests, starts a gateway, invokes a provider, or ports batch/cron prefill behavior in the same pass.
The slice accepts arbitrary objects by silently stringifying them; malformed entries must degrade visibly and safely.
The slice exposes prompt contents in telemetry or error messages.

Algorithm: iterate the four Hermes Nous bucket tags ("requests", "requests-1h", "tokens", "tokens-1h") via the paired x-ratelimit-remaining-{tag} and x-ratelimit-reset-{tag} headers; use headers.Get, strings.TrimSpace, strconv.Atoi for remaining, strconv.ParseFloat for reset seconds. If at least one bucket parsed successfully and none are exhausted, return RateLimitUpstreamCapacity. Otherwise return RateLimitInsufficientEvidence. STEP 4: no shared breaker state, no time.Now, no sleeps, no retry policy, and no provider routing changes; imports are limited to net/http, strconv, and strings (plus testing in the test file).

Define `type GuardState struct { LastKnownClass RateLimitClass; LastKnownAt time.Time; Unavailable bool }` and `func ApplyClassification(state GuardState, now time.Time, class RateLimitClass) GuardState`. items.name: Capability-based model tier routing
items.contract: Route simple queries to cheap models and complex queries to capable models based on a fast classifier. Avoids sending 'hello' to Claude Opus and avoids sending multi-file refactors to a 7B model.

not_ready_when: Only one model tier available
acceptance: Simple queries (greetings, single-file edits) route to cheap tier
Complex queries (multi-file refactor, architecture) route to capable tier

Operator can override classifier with explicit model selection
Classification failures fall back to capable tier (safe default)
done_signal: Capability router tests prove simple queries hit cheap tier and complex queries hit capable tier
items.note: Complete: internal/hermes/capability_router.go classifies simple versus complex requests with deterministic local signals and routes them to configured cheap or capable tiers while preserving context cancellation/error propagation.

evidence.tests: go test ./internal/hermes -run TestCapabilityRouter -count=1
evidence.note: Capability router fixtures prove simple greetings choose the cheap tier, complex and long requests choose the capable tier, and request context propagates to the selected client.

items.name: Docker backend top-level container reuse semantics
items.contract: Pure helper internal/tools/docker_container_key.go exposes type DockerContainerRequest struct{TaskID string; IsSubagent bool; IsRollout bool} and DockerContainerKey(req DockerContainerRequest) string. items.name: Go-native Hermes web_crawl tool adapter
items.contract: Gormes exposes a Go-native `web_crawl` tool for the Hermes `web_crawl_tool` helper surface, backed by the existing fakeable `WebHTTPClient` and web backend resolver. Firecrawl crawl posts to `/v2/crawl` with Hermes' fixed 20-page markdown crawl payload and ignores instructions because Firecrawl crawl has no prompt parameter. Tavily crawl posts to `/crawl` with `url`, `limit`, `extract_depth`, optional `instructions`, and the API key in the JSON body. Provider HTTP failures return a redacted crawl error without leaking bearer tokens.

items.name: Browser session inactivity cleanup thread
items.contract: Gormes mirrors Hermes' browser session inactivity cleanup: a background goroutine reaps sessions that have been idle longer than BROWSER_SESSION_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT (default 300s, overridable via GORMES_BROWSER_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT env var). Cleanup closes the harness process for timed-out sessions and records redacted inactivity_cleanup evidence. The goroutine starts once at manager/service init and sleeps between reap cycles (default 60s interval) using a clock seam so tests stay hermetic.

items.name: MCP circuit breaker cooldown + reconnect reset
items.contract: MCP tool calls maintain Hermes-compatible per-server recovery state: repeated call failures trip a circuit breaker, calls before cooldown short-circuit without touching the session, the first call after cooldown is a half-open probe, probe success closes the breaker, probe failure reopens it, and a successful OAuth reconnect clears stale breaker counts even if the immediate post-reconnect retry still fails.

items.name: Auth state TOCTOU close + redaction default-on parity
items.contract: Gormes auth.json read-modify-write paths use atomic file replacement (open, write to sibling tempfile, fsync, rename) with no observable TOCTOU window between read and write. MCP OAuth credential persistence follows the same atomic-replace contract. The redaction default is restored to ON; opt-out is via explicit `redaction.enabled: false` in config. Mirrors Hermes v0.13.0 PRs #21193 (redaction default-on flip), #21194 (auth.json TOCTOU), #21241 (MCP OAuth TOCTOU). Reverts the v0.12.0 default-off flip (#16794).
items.degraded_mode: Without atomic replace, a concurrent read can observe a partially-written auth.json and crash the session; with the atomic-replace contract the read either sees the prior valid state or the new valid state, never a partial merge. Without redaction default-on, log capture, debug bundles, and trajectory writes leak credentials by default.

not_ready_when: Atomic replace is implemented only on Linux without portable handling for darwin/windows tempfile rename semantics.
Redaction default-on is enforced silently without surfacing the operator-visible config knob `redaction.enabled: false`.
Tests use sleeps to trigger the TOCTOU window instead of a fake-fs/fake-clock.
MCP OAuth persistence still uses non-atomic write while auth.json is fixed in the same slice (split if needed).

items.name: Symlink-preserving atomic writer helper
items.contract: Gormes adds a shared atomic replace helper that matches Hermes' symlink-safe config/state writes: regular files are atomically replaced, existing symlinks remain symlinks while their real targets receive the new bytes, broken symlinks create the target without replacing the link, and existing target permissions are preserved unless the caller explicitly supplies first-write permissions.
items.degraded_mode: Permission-denied, symlink-loop, outside-root, temp-file, chmod, and rename failures return typed atomic_write_failed or atomic_write_symlink_escape evidence without deleting the original target, replacing the symlink, or leaking private absolute home paths.
ready_when: The worker can implement and test the helper under t.TempDir with ordinary files, live symlinks, broken symlinks, and permission fixtures; no private config home or live gateway state is needed.
The first migration scope is limited to Gormes config.toml writes, setup tools config writes, secrets-runtime snapshots, and session index mirror writes.
Existing config/security/session tests are green before the helper migration.

The helper replaces a symlink path with a regular file, follows symlinks outside the caller-approved root, or changes existing target permission bits unexpectedly.
Tests depend on platform-specific privileged chmod behavior without skip guards.

items.name: File write/patch staleness registry + cwd tracking
items.contract: Gormes write_file and patch match Hermes' stateful file-edit safety: every read records a per-root path token, hash/mtime/size evidence, and live cwd/task context; write_file and patch reject stale edits when the file changed since the last read token; relative paths use the active terminal cwd/task cwd at operation time; successful writes update the registry; missing files, first writes, and external deletions return deterministic evidence without corrupting content.

ready_when: Native file task tool surface is complete, including root-confined read_file, write_file, patch, and search_files.
Terminal cwd config bridge is complete enough to provide a deterministic active cwd for relative path resolution.
Tests can run entirely in t.TempDir with injected clocks and fake cwd/task IDs; no shell, provider, checkpoint, or live Hermes process is required.
not_ready_when: The slice implements checkpoint restore, syntax lint, PTY/background terminal process state, or whole-file sync-back in the same pass.

items.name: Hermes Kanban dispatcher and worker spawn loop
items.contract: Gormes ports the Hermes Kanban dispatcher core as a native gateway-managed loop with a fakeable worker-spawner seam: each tick reclaims stale claims, selects ready assigned tasks, claims through the store, records spawn attempts and spawn failures, passes GORMES_* worker context, respects max-spawn caps across successful and failed attempts, and blocks tasks behind a circuit breaker after repeated failures. Real OS process spawning, PID/crash detection, max-runtime termination, worker log rotation, and production config wiring remain a separate row.

not_ready_when: The slice shells out to Hermes Python, reads live Hermes profile config, or starts real workers in unit tests.
A crashed worker leaves a task permanently running with no TTL reclaim evidence.

acceptance: Dispatcher fixtures prove dry-run output, ready-task selection, max-spawn caps, and no-op behavior when no ready tasks exist.
Stale-claim fixtures prove expired running tasks return to ready with reclaim evidence.
Spawn fixtures prove worker env includes the Gormes task id, board path, assignee/profile, and workspace details without leaking other agents' config.
Failure fixtures prove retry counts, failed-spawn recovery, and circuit breaker block after the configured failure limit.
Gateway lifecycle fixtures prove the dispatcher is owned by the gateway loop and can be nudged without starting duplicate daemons.
items.note: Complete: TDD landed the fakeable dispatcher core and gateway-owned lifecycle seam. The gateway Manager owns an injectable Kanban dispatcher loop with deterministic tick/nudge channels, runtime status JSON evidence, degraded last_error handling that does not crash the gateway, exact trigger timestamps, clean shutdown, restart-after-stop ownership release, and closed test-channel shutdown protection. items.name: Kanban worker heartbeat, reclaim, and zombie detection
items.contract: Kanban workers emit a heartbeat at a configurable interval; the dispatcher reclaims tasks whose worker heartbeat is stale beyond the threshold, marks the worker as zombie, and re-enqueues the task with retry budget honored. Auto-block on incomplete worker exit, darwin zombie detection, and a unified failure counter across spawn/timeout/crash outcomes are part of the same contract. Mirrors Hermes v0.13.0 PRs #21183, #21214, #20188, #20410.
items.degraded_mode: Without heartbeat reclaim, a hung worker holds its task forever and the dispatcher cannot reassign; status reports show worker=stale and task=held with last-seen timestamp instead of pretending the work is in progress.
ready_when: 5.M `Hermes Kanban dispatcher and worker spawn loop` is complete and exposes a worker-state seam reachable from tests.
2.E.3 `Durable worker supervisor status seam` heartbeat states (no-worker, healthy, stale, supervisor-unavailable) are present and reusable.
Fake clock and fake worker controllers exist in tests so heartbeat timing can be exercised without real subprocesses.
not_ready_when: The slice spawns real worker subprocesses to test heartbeat timing.
Reclaim path silently drops a task's retry budget when promoting it back to the queue.
Zombie detection collapses with healthy-but-slow workers because the threshold is not configurable.
darwin-specific detection is hidden behind unconditional Linux-only assumptions.
unblocks: Kanban hallucination gate for worker-created-card claims
Kanban worker auto-block on incomplete exit
acceptance: TestKanbanWorker_HeartbeatStaleReclaim proves a worker whose heartbeat exceeds threshold is marked zombie and its task is re-enqueued with the retry budget decremented exactly once.
TestKanbanWorker_HeartbeatHealthyDoesNotReclaim proves an active worker is never reclaimed.
TestKanbanWorker_FailureCounterUnified proves spawn-failure, timeout, and crash each increment the same counter and reflect in dispatcher status.
TestKanbanWorker_DarwinZombieDetected proves darwin-specific PID-state detection runs on darwin and returns 'unknown' on other GOOS without panicking.
done_signal: Heartbeat reclaim, zombie marking, unified failure counter, and darwin-specific detection are fixture-proven with a fake clock; no test launches a real worker subprocess.
items.note: Complete 2026-05-07: TDD landed heartbeat extension (HeartbeatTask now extends claim_expires by heartbeatTTL), zombie detection and reclaim (ReclaimStaleHeartbeats based on heartbeat_at staleness), unified failure counter (IncrementFailureCounter with FailureKind{spawn,timeout,crash}), auto-block on incomplete exit (AutoBlockIncompleteExit), darwin PID-state zombie detection (zombie_darwin.go via syscall.Kill), and cross-platform stub (zombie_other.go). All 8 acceptance tests pass over an in-memory SQLite store with fake clock injection. Source: Hermes v0.13.0 (v2026.5.7) Kanban worker-reliability PRs — #21183 (heartbeat/reclaim/zombie/retry-cap), #21214 (auto-block on incomplete exit), #20188 (darwin zombie detection), #20410 (unified failure counter).

items.name: Cron run resource release contract
items.contract: internal/cron exposes a typed per-run resource-release ledger helper that records spawned subprocess PIDs (via an injected killer interface), io.Closer values for SQLite session DBs, and outbound HTTP RoundTripper idle-closables. The helper guarantees deterministic close ordering, idempotent re-entry, partial-failure continuation, and explicit evidence vocabulary so a later Executor binding can release every per-run resource exactly once. The helper does not start a kernel turn, hit a provider, manage MCP stdio runtimes, or change the Scheduler goroutine lifecycle.

items.name: Gormes mcp login browser callback flow
items.contract: Implements `MCPLoginFlow.Login` over a localhost callback server (ephemeral `http.Server` bound to 127.0.0.1 with an OS-assigned port), a browser launch hook (default `os.exec` opens the system browser; tests inject a recording fake), and a code-for-token exchange transport (tests inject a fake `http.RoundTripper` so no live token endpoint is contacted). On success, the resulting MCP session is stored through row 15458's interface; on failure, the OAuth state store is left byte-identical. Donor pattern (pattern-only, not copied verbatim): `references/go-agent-os/goclaw/internal/oauth/openai.go` localhost-callback shape; donor pattern (Hermes-side): `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/auth.py:_make_spotify_callback_handler`.
items.degraded_mode: Port collision returns `mcp_login_port_collision`; callback timeout returns `mcp_login_callback_timeout`; token exchange error returns `mcp_login_token_exchange_failed`; redirect-URI mismatch returns `mcp_login_redirect_uri_mismatch`. None of these failure modes panic, hang, or leak access tokens / refresh tokens / authorization codes into stdout/stderr.

items.name: CLI log snapshot reader using shared redactor
items.contract: internal/cli/log_snapshot.go exposes type LogClass string with constants LogClassMain="main" and LogClassToolAudit="tool_audit", type LogSnapshotRoots struct{LogPath, ToolAuditPath string}, type SnapshotOpts struct{HeadBytes, TailBytes int64} (zero or negative HeadBytes/TailBytes default to 64*1024 and 16*1024 respectively), type LogSection struct{Class LogClass; Path string; Head, Tail []byte; Missing, Truncated bool; Redacted int; Unreadable string} and type Snapshot struct{Sections []LogSection}. SnapshotLogs(roots LogSnapshotRoots, opts SnapshotOpts) Snapshot returns Sections in order [LogClassMain, LogClassToolAudit] and ALWAYS includes both sections even when both files are absent. For each path: if os.Stat fails with os.IsNotExist, set Missing=true and skip read. If os.ReadFile fails for any other reason, set Unreadable to err.Error() and continue. If file size <= HeadBytes+TailBytes, set Head to the entire file content, Tail to nil, Truncated=false. If file size > HeadBytes+TailBytes, set Head to the first HeadBytes bytes, Tail to the last TailBytes bytes, Truncated=true. Then split each of Head and Tail by '\n' (bytes.Split), pass each non-empty line through RedactLine, sum the returned counts into LogSection.Redacted, and write the redacted lines back joined by '\n' into Head/Tail. The function never returns an error and never panics.

items.name: Install isolation: GORMES_BIN_DIR is an authoritative sandbox boundary
items.contract: When `GORMES_BIN_DIR` (or `--bin-dir`) is set to a directory the operator intends as a sandbox, install.sh must publish the gormes command only into that directory and must NOT also rewrite an existing `gormes` binary discovered elsewhere on PATH (typically `~/.local/bin/gormes`). The current behavior emits `updating active PATH command /home/<user>/.local/bin/gormes` and replaces a production symlink with one pointing at the sandbox, which dangles when the sandbox dir is reaped. Sandbox passes must be observably side-effect-free outside the sandbox prefix.
items.degraded_mode: Without this fix, any operator running install.sh with a sandbox bin dir (e.g., for testing, in a container, in CI) silently mutates the host's production gormes symlink. The gormes-install skill flags this as iso-bin-hijack on every sandbox pass.
ready_when: An installtest harness exists that can exec `sh install.sh` in a temp HOME with isolated PATH and assert on post-state.
install.sh exposes the active-PATH-command-update logic in a function reachable from a shell-level test.
not_ready_when: The fix removes the convenient default behavior of updating an existing PATH-discovered gormes binary on a normal upgrade install (default invocation, no sandbox env vars).
The slice changes the public default install path or the operator-facing flags in a backwards-incompatible way without a migration note.
Tests rely on touching the real `~/.local/bin/gormes` symlink instead of a temp HOME with isolated PATH.

TestInstall_DefaultBinDir_StillUpdatesPathBinary preserves the convenient default behavior: with no sandbox env vars, install.sh DOES update an existing PATH-discovered gormes symlink so upgrade-in-place still works.

items.name: Install isolation: skip system service install when sandbox bin dir is set
items.contract: When the operator declares a sandbox boundary by setting GORMES_BIN_DIR or GORMES_PREFIX, install.sh must not write to the production user systemd unit dir (~/.config/systemd/user/gormes-gateway.service) or the production launchd plist dir (~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.gormes.gateway.plist). Today the print_service_instructions dispatcher unconditionally writes those files with ExecStart pointing at the SANDBOX binary path, so the operator's gateway service silently breaks once /tmp is reaped. The same sandbox_bin_dir_set helper used for iso-bin-hijack and iso-shellrc-leak gates the dispatcher with an early-return + clear log line. print_install_plan_body and print_verbose_plan surface the decision as `install_system_service: skipped|yes`.
items.degraded_mode: Without this fix, every sandboxed install pass on a Linux host with systemd-user available silently rewrites the operator's production gormes-gateway.service to point ExecStart at /tmp/gormes-install-test/<ts>/home/bin/gormes. After the next /tmp reap or reboot, the gateway service fails to start because its binary path no longer exists. Same shape as iso-bin-hijack but worse — the failure is invisible until the operator tries to use the gateway.

items.name: Install: prefer pre-built release binary over source build by default
items.contract: install.sh defaults to fetching the pre-built release tarball from GitHub Releases (gormes-<version>-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz + .sha256) instead of cloning + go-building from source. Decision is exposed via the dry-run plan as `install_method: binary-fetch|source-build (<reason>)`. Source-build is used when: --local is set, --from-source / GORMES_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE=1, --branch is non-default (release binaries only published from main), or the host platform (uname -s/-m) has no published asset slug. On binary-fetch failure (network, missing asset, SHA-256 mismatch, missing tools), install.sh falls back to source-build with a clear log line so installs still succeed in restricted environments.
items.degraded_mode: Without this fix, every fresh `curl https://gormes.ai/install.sh | bash` downloads a Go toolchain (~150MB), clones the source repo, and runs go build — typically 2-5 minutes even on a fast machine, and impossible at all on locked-down hosts without a Go compiler or git. With the fix, the same fresh install completes in ~2 seconds via signed binary fetch.
ready_when: v0.1.06 release publishes 18 assets (linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64 .tar.gz + .sha256 + SBOM) so the binary-fetch path has artifacts to download.

items.name: Channel/TUI iteration-limit finalization transcript fixture
items.contract: Add an end-to-end visible transcript fixture for Hermes-style max-tool-iteration exhaustion across kernel, gateway, and local TUI renderers. When the tool loop reaches the budget, Gormes must ask the provider for a single no-tools summary, deliver one final assistant message, clear live tool-progress/thinking indicators, and never expose raw loop-control errors such as `tool iteration limit exceeded`, duplicate final answers, or a stuck hourglass/progress row.
items.degraded_mode: If the no-tools summary request fails, the visible final transcript uses a bounded degraded summary-failed message with provider error classification, not a raw loop panic or repeated progress bubble.
ready_when: Kernel tool loop is complete and requestMaxIterationSummary is validated with a toolless provider request.
Gateway stream/tool trace formatting fixture matrix is complete so progress messages are separate from final assistant text.
The worker can drive fake kernel frames or a fake provider through gateway/TUI renderers without live channels, providers, Telegram API calls, or a Bubble Tea Program.
not_ready_when: The slice changes the 90-iteration default or removes the Hermes summary-request text.
The slice relies on real provider latency, live channel delivery, screenshots, or sleeps instead of fake events/clocked coalescer fixtures.
The slice accepts a final transcript containing raw loop-control text, duplicate assistant final text, or lingering progress after finalization.
acceptance: TestIterationLimitFinalization_GatewaySendsOneSummaryFinal drives a fake budget-exhausted turn and proves gateway output contains one final assistant message, no raw iteration-limit error, and no duplicate final send/edit fallback.
TestIterationLimitFinalization_ToolProgressClearedAfterFinal proves the channel progress message is finalized/cleared before the assistant final transcript is considered complete.
TestIterationLimitFinalization_SummaryFailureIsBoundedDegradedText proves provider failure during the no-tools summary path yields one bounded degraded final message and no red loop-control bubble.
TestHermesBehavioralFidelity_FinalAssistantNotDuplicated proves local TUI output renders the summary once from history and not again from DraftText or live streaming state.
Existing kernel tests for DefaultMaxToolIterations=90 and toolless summary requests remain green.
items.note: Added by the 2026-05-04 behavioral parity audit. The kernel loop and gateway tool-progress rows are already complete, but the user-visible failure mode spans kernel summary, gateway coalescing, tool-progress cleanup, and TUI draft/history rendering; this row lives in Phase 5.Q so the already-shipped Phase 2 gateway lane stays closed while the remaining visible transcript fidelity work is tracked with TUI/API behavior. 2026-05-06 all-topic parity sweep confirmed Kernel tool loop, Gateway stream/tool trace formatting fixture matrix, and Native TUI Hermes bottom-pinned chrome layout are complete, then promoted this row to P0 as the next builder-ready channel/TUI/tool-loop fidelity slice. items.name: Transactional tool execution with snapshot/rollback
items.contract: Wrap uncertain in-process tool calls with a bounded workspace filesystem snapshot before execution; successful calls commit by discarding the snapshot, while failed calls restore modified, deleted, and newly-created files before the executor returns.
ready_when: Pre-execution command classification is complete and marks uncertain tool requests as RequiresSnapshot.
The slice can use temp workspace fixtures and in-process fake tools; no live sandbox backend, shadow git repo, or provider credentials are required.
not_ready_when: The implementation tries to replace Hermes' full shadow-git checkpoint history, CLI /rollback UX, or sandbox isolation-depth policy in the same pass.
Rollback follows symlinks outside the workspace root, preserves new files created by failed tools, or deletes pre-existing files that should be restored.
acceptance: Uncertain tool calls create a workspace snapshot before invoking the inner executor.
Failed uncertain tool calls restore modified file content, restore files deleted during the call, and remove files created during the call.
Successful uncertain tool calls commit by preserving filesystem changes and reporting no rollback.
Safe tool calls do not pay snapshot cost, and unsafe tool calls remain blocked without touching the inner executor.
Rollback failures are returned as degraded executor errors instead of being hidden behind the tool failure.
done_signal: Transactional executor tests prove rollback on failure and commit on success with filesystem integrity

Tests can use fake review runners and fake stores; no live provider, Telegram, gateway, or shell command is required.
not_ready_when: The slice grants terminal, browser, file-write outside skill_manage, provider-management, or foreground subagent toolsets to the background fork.

acceptance: TestBackgroundReviewFork_InheritsActiveRuntime proves provider, model, api_mode, base_url, api_key, credential pool, platform, parent_session_id, and memory store flags are copied from the active parent into the fake review worker.

items.note: Complete: TDD expanded `internal/goncho/importance_scorer.go` so ranking uses `α·recency + β·effective_importance + γ·relevance`, where effective importance is the agent-assigned importance after recency decay. `internal/goncho/decay.go` adds retention review candidates with summarize/forget actions for old low-effective-importance memories. `LocalMarkdownMemoryStore.Retrieve` now ranks active scoped memories through the shared scorer instead of raw SQL importance ordering, while retaining nonmatching memories in storage. `update_memory` now accepts optional `importance` so the agent can promote or demote entries after storage; descriptors expose the same field. items.note: Complete: TDD replaced placeholder word-deletion mutation with a deterministic GEPA-style optimizer. `GenerateVariants` creates bounded strategy mutations for exact tool selection, concrete response quality, task decomposition, and command safety. `OptimizeDetailed` scores every variant through the prompt evaluation harness, promotes the best variant as the next iteration base only when it clears the improvement threshold, records per-iteration candidates/evaluations/selected variant, and terminates with explicit converged, perfect_score, or budget_exhausted evidence. items.name: Windows install.ps1 release binary fetch selector
items.contract: The native Windows installer defaults to fetching the latest prebuilt `windows-amd64` or `windows-arm64` release archive from GitHub Releases on `main`, verifies the `.sha256` sidecar, extracts `gormes.exe` into the managed build-bin path, and then reuses the existing publish, PATH, verification, ledger, and gateway-restart flow. It falls back to the managed source build only when `-FromSource` or `GORMES_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE` is set, the branch is not `main`, the host architecture has no published asset, or runtime release download/verification fails.
items.degraded_mode: Without the Windows release-fetch selector, the v1 Windows-without-Python promise is still source-build shaped: fresh Windows installs need Git plus Go even though CI publishes Windows release archives.

items.name: Release build-date provenance injection
items.contract: The release workflow injects a UTC build timestamp into every prebuilt binary, and `gormes version --json` reports it as build_date beside the semver tag, Hermes-style date alias, git commit, dirty bit, Go runtime, OS, and arch. Developer/source builds may fall back to Go VCS build-info time or `unknown`, but tagged release artifacts must carry the workflow-injected timestamp.

Resolver tests prove ldflags-injected BuildDate wins, VCS build-info time is a fallback, and missing metadata returns `unknown` instead of an empty string.
TestReleaseWorkflowInjectsBuildDateProvenance proves the release workflow computes BUILD_DATE in UTC and passes `-X main.BuildDate=${BUILD_DATE}` in the build ldflags.

items.contract: The autonomous builder loop records a cost-per-iteration estimate in its status file (loop-health.env or a sibling file), broken down by backend (codexu vs opencode/<model>), accumulated daily and monthly.
